headline: No - pressure caps output below 25 MGD

highlights.text: First limit: feed pressure at 75.9 bar ceiling, only ~0.42 recovery vs 0.60 target
High-pressure pump at discharge ceiling 75.9 bar, 100% utilised
Lower-recovery workaround needs ~60 MGD intake vs 42 MGD concept
Preheat to ~80F helps per study but alone does not close gap in model

summary: At 60 F and 49,000 mg/L the model reaches only 0.42 recovery at the 75.9 bar ceiling versus 0.60 target, so 5 available trains make about 17.5 MGD not 25 MGD. First limits are RO-201 membrane pressure and P-201 discharge pressure both at 100%. Cheapest lasting fix is added parallel seawater train capacity with its own pump.
request: Can this 25 MGD concept hold about 60 percent overall recovery and the finished-water duty on the cold, salty corner of the ship-channel record (about 60 F and 49,000 mg/L TDS) with one seawater train out of service? What limits it first, and what is the cheapest way to stay at 25 MGD?
